raw_response:
I am old and I have only been doing this one year, so I follow what my neighbors do and keep things simple. My back is not what it would be on a young man, and not all my family is around to help — some of my children work in the city. I cannot afford to lose money on inputs that don't work, so I stay conservative.

In Quzhou we always do wheat and maize on the same land — wheat in winter, maize after the June harvest. That is what everyone does here. I put 3 mu into that rotation. Cotton is a cash crop my neighbor grows and he told me it pays well, so I put 2 mu into cotton. Stevia the village extension worker said is a new contract crop — buyers come collect it — so I try 1 mu to see how it goes. That fills my 6 mu.

For seeds, I buy the improved wheat and hybrid maize that the supply cooperative sells — first year I did that and it worked fine, so I do it again. For cotton I use Bt hybrid seed because that's what's sold in town and it cuts down on the worm spraying. For stevia I buy seedlings from the contract company.

I am not confident with fertilizer rates so I ask my neighbor what he uses and I copy that. I don't go above what he says because I don't want to burn the crop. Irrigation — I have the well so I use it, but electricity costs money, so I only pump when the soil looks dry or the crop shows stress. Tillage I hire a rotary tiller for everything because I cannot do it myself at my age.
